why: A freshly initialized repository, with the tree in the index and no commit, is a legitimate state — and it makes `git log` exit 128. The N/A branch exists because the alternative is the `catch` that swallowed the error and returned an empty string, and an empty string has no co-authorship trailer: the repository with no history PASSED a rule about history. A crash becoming a pass is the same class of defect that `git()` documents. The `pass` side declares `"commits": []` and has to come out N/A; the `fail` side has the trailer and keeps failing, so the guard did not switch the rule off.
